about: The AI apps an owner may connect to TinyAssets, as data (autoconnect_research.md section 2.3): one entry per vendor, so no code names one. match names how a signed-in client is known: hosts, the host of a Client ID Metadata Document's URL (verified: the authorization server fetched the document from there), or names, a word of the client's self-declared name (unverified); redirects, the URIs its client sends access to (an https URI or a custom scheme's, a path prefix when it ends with /, a loopback one matched on any port), read from the vendor's own page. A CIMD client is verified only when its document's host and every redirect it registered are that app's.  registration is how its client registers with our sign-in: cimd, or dcr for a vendor that offers no CIMD (the founder's ruling, 2026-11-04: the one pre-login exception to no anonymous traffic, on only while DCR_ENABLED is true, and then only for a client whose name names a dcr vendor and whose every redirect is that vendor's: a dcr vendor with no redirects recorded yet has dynamic registration off, until the live test reads them). connect is what the user does in that app: a link, a sentence to send (say), steps, and text to copy (code). The say sentence is the user's own request, typed in their own chat as the connect act itself, so it may ask the vendor's agent to save the TinyAssets skill (autoconnect_research.md section 2.3); text TinyAssets serves to an agent (the MCP instructions, tool descriptions, the plugins) never asks an agent to save to its memory or install anything (doors/guards/apps.test.ts holds the split). Each entry names the vendor page its steps were read from and when. One source for the public connect page (WebSite/site-react/app/connect), the owner app's connected apps page and agents_list's apps (each app's connect_url).

steps: Open the link while signed in to Claude: it opens the custom connector dialog with TinyAssets filled in.
Select Add, then Connect, and sign in to TinyAssets.
Claude Duet, Cowork and the Claude apps share your account's connectors, so this connects them too.
On chatgpt.com in a browser, open Plugins and select the plus button, then Add custom MCP server.
Name it TinyAssets and enter the server address https://tinyassets.io/mcp, with OAuth.
Review the warning, select I understand and want to continue, then Create as a plugin.
Install the plugin and sign in to TinyAssets. Dots use the plugins installed for your account.
For Codex in a terminal, run the two commands below instead.
connect.code:
codex mcp add TinyAssets --url https://tinyassets.io/mcp
codex mcp login TinyAssets

apps.name: Gemini
surfaces: Gemini on the web and mobile

steps: On gemini.google.com in a browser, open Settings, then Connected Apps, then Add a custom app.
Enter the server address https://tinyassets.io/mcp and sign in to TinyAssets.
Gemini offers custom apps on a personal Google account, to people 18 or older in the US, with Keep Activity on.
To make sure Gemini uses it in a chat, type @ and pick TinyAssets.
In Cursor, add a remote MCP server with the address https://tinyassets.io/mcp, or put the text below in .cursor/mcp.json.
Sign in to TinyAssets when Cursor asks.
